name: Estonia
headline: Estonia: +1.3% growth in 2025, 4.8% inflation, debt 24% of GDP
sections: Estonia is a $47.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 102nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.3% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $52K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 10.8% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.8% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 19.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 7.4% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 19.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 24% of GDP (2025), a low level that has risen from 19% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.0% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +0.3% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 156% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were −2.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 43% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 79.3 years (2024). Population: 1.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
